decisions.text: type pie: fractions of the total are the message: a pie, which shows ½, ⅓ and ¼ at a glance and announces the whole (G1.36)
slices largest first, clockwise from 12 o'clock: Southeast, Northwest, Southwest, Midwest, Mid-Atlantic, West
each slice its own colour, handed out in slice order (D-22 (a)): Southeast series-1, Northwest series-2, Southwest series-3, Midwest series-4, Mid-Atlantic series-5, West series-6
each slice named outside it, its value under the name, formatted as one set (G7.27, D-51 (ii)): $288K, $279K, $248K, $220K, $188K, $69K
no outlines: true gaps 1.0 pt wide between the slices (G7.26s: 0.7 % of the diameter)

source.shows: the regions as unordered parts, so a categorical palette, a hue each, where the book's bad version shades them in one blue at random and the darker slices seem to hold more of something (G4.6, G4.8 [L]); six parts, a pie's comfortable most (D-23), the sixth in the palette's purple; the values hidden to thousands as one set, $288K for $287,735 (R5-10, G6.12). The bad version cannot be asked for: colours are the style's and the parts' kind the data's
